title: UlaCache: Unified Logical Addressing for Sparse LLM Serving
summary: UlaCache replaces conventional physically-tied KV cache management with a unified logical address space spanning GPU and optional CPU memory, combined with a Parallel Bucketed LRU for shared GPU pool eviction, so sparse-attention KV selection is decoupled from physical placement. The cost is substantial systems complexity: address-mapping infrastructure, CPU-GPU transfer coordination, local buffer management across decoding steps, and integration with sparse attention and speculative decoding, with gains demonstrated only on H200 and B300 hardware in DP/TP configurations. It can fail when the workload does not already use sparse attention and speculative decoding, when transfer bandwidth between CPU and GPU becomes the bottleneck, or when the reader's single 24 GB GPU cannot realize the distributed-storage benefits the system is designed around.
rationale: The reported gains depend on sparse attention, speculative decoding, DP/TP serving, and datacenter GPUs, none of which match a single 24 GB GPU or API-based production setup, so this is worth monitoring rather than adopting.
technique: Unified logical addressing for sparse KV cache management

claims.statement: UlaCache replaces conventional physically-tied KV cache management with a unified logical address space spanning GPU and optional CPU memory, combined with a Parallel Bucketed LRU for shared GPU pool eviction, so sparse-attention KV selection is decoupled from physical placement. The cost is substantial systems complexity: address-mapping infrastructure, CPU-GPU transfer coordination, local buffer management across decoding steps, and integration with sparse attention and speculative decoding, with gains demonstrated only on H200 and B300 hardware in DP/TP configurations. It can fail when the workload does not already use sparse attention and speculative decoding, when transfer bandwidth between CPU and GPU becomes the bottleneck, or when the reader's single 24 GB GPU cannot realize the distributed-storage benefits the system is designed around.

Peak decoding throughput speedups of 1.16x (DP) and 1.70x (TP) on H200, and 1.73x (DP) and 2.51x (TP) on B300, with speculative decoding enabled under matched CPU and GPU memory budgets, versus a state-of-the-art baseline.
